conventions.convention: kθ has rows (cos θ, sin θ) and (−sin θ, cos θ); a_t=diag(e^(t/2),e^(−t/2)); dk=dθ/(2π). The parabolic character δ_P(a_t)=e^t is the inverse of the group modular function Δ_P(a_t)=e^(−t).
I(ε,ν) has left P-covariance δ_P^(1/2)σεe^ν and right translation; e^ν(a_t)=e^(νt/2). Allowed K-weights satisfy r≡ε mod 2, and the exceptional parameter lattice consists of integers ν≡ε+1 mod 2.
W=−iJ and E±=(H±iS)/2; real directions are differentiated first and then complexified. The Killing-form quadratic Casimir is Ω=W²/8−W/4+E+E−/2 and has principal-series scalar (ν²−1)/8.

The intertwiner uses w=k_(−π/2), opposite to Kerr's Weyl matrix, so changing that matrix contributes (−1)^ε. The initial integral requires Re ν>0. Its actual normalization base is c0 in even parity and c1 in odd parity; odd-parity c0 is only a formal scalar.

D_n^- is the holomorphic inverse-action model with K-weights −(n+2j); D_n^+ is its antiholomorphic conjugate with weights +(n+2j). The superscripts label weight signs, while the principal-series module symbols M use a different superscript convention.
The fixed Haar measure has radial density 2π sinh(t) dt for a_t=diag(e^(t/2),e^(−t/2)); it gives extremal discrete-series coefficient squared integral 4π/(n−1).

Divisor support is locally finite, hence finite on compact X. Zero germs have order +∞, but principal divisors require nonzero functions. L(D) imposes ord_p(f)≥−D(p). If (u)=D'−D, the identification L(D)→L(D') is multiplication by 1/u.

O(D) has transitions g_ij=f_i/f_j, frames e_j=g_ij e_i, and canonical meromorphic section s_D=f_i e_i. Bundle-section evaluation and zero order use the regular coefficient h f_i, even when the representing meromorphic function h has a pole.

A finite good cover is supplied, rather than universally asserted to exist, and must be subordinate to holomorphic frame domains for the fixed-cover comparison. Global sheaf–Dolbeault comparison requires no good-cover hypothesis.

The ordered Čech differential is δb_ij=b_j−b_i. The degree-one Dolbeault identification is normalized to send this splitting to [∂̄b_i], the negative of the unnormalized total-complex identification. The residue pairing is (2πi)^(−1)∫θ∧ω with θ first.

Projective space parametrizes lines. A linear system maps canonically to P(V*); a coordinate basis change acts projectively on its image. O(1) is the dual tautological bundle, and its pullback is the original divisor bundle.

Full AC is explicitly retained for unitary-dual, disintegration, derived-cohomology and Hodge uses. The general noncompact O(D) construction uses countable choice; its compact finite-cover branch and the explicit Veronese example are choice-free.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and the stated compact-picture conventions. L_W f_n=n f_n and L_E± f_n=(1+ν±n)f_(n±2)/2. These operators preserve smooth and K-finite vectors and satisfy [L_W,L_E±]=±2L_E± and [L_E+,L_E−]=L_W.

Assume full AC. For compact X of topological genus g and every divisor D, the relevant spaces are finite-dimensional, i(D)=h⁰(X,K_X⊗O(D)*), and ℓ(D)−h⁰(X,K_X⊗O(D)*)=deg D+1−g. A nonzero meromorphic differential exists; for any such η, i(D)=ℓ(K_η−D) and ℓ(D)−ℓ(K_η−D)=deg D+1−g.

Assume AC and real ν. The full spherical K-finite module admits a positive-definite invariant Hermitian form if and only if |ν|<1. For 0<|ν|<1 the displayed Fourier form completes to the irreducible strongly continuous unitary spherical complementary series; ν=0 gives the spherical unitary principal series. No full odd module at real ν≠0 admits a positive-definite invariant form.

Assume AC. Outside W_ε, I^K_(ε,ν) is algebraically irreducible, its L² compact picture is irreducible, and its smooth compact picture is topologically irreducible. At positive n∈W_ε the two one-sided tails form the unique maximal proper submodule and L_(n−1) is the unique irreducible quotient; at −n the finite module is the unique irreducible submodule and the tails form the quotient. I^K_(1,0) splits into the two odd limit chains. The Casimir scalar is (ν²−1)/8 and determines the central character up to parameter sign.

Assume AC, compact X, a holomorphic line bundle E and supplied compatible metrics. The two-term smooth Dolbeault sheaf resolution is exact; H¹(X,O_X(E)) is the smooth quotient Ω^(0,1)(X,E)/∂̄_EΩ^(0,0)(X,E), H⁰ is the holomorphic-section space, and H^q=0 for q≥2. A supplied frame-subordinate finite good cover has canonical Leray comparison isomorphisms in every degree, compatible with refinement.

Assume full AC, compact X and divisor D. The residue pairing on H¹(X,O(D))×H⁰(X,K_X⊗O(D)*) is perfect and induces complex-linear isomorphisms with the respective dual spaces. For any supplied nonzero meromorphic differential η, i(D)=ℓ(K_η−D). The pairing is natural for divisor inclusions and compatible with linear equivalence. H¹(X,K_X)*≅H⁰(X,O_X) and h¹(X,K_X)=1.

Assume AC. Every irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation of SL₂(R) is equivalent to exactly one of: the trivial representation; I_(ε,is) with s≥0 excluding (ε,s)=(1,0); D_n^± for n≥2; D_1^±; or I_(0,ν) with 0<ν<1. The principal sign parameters are identified. Every irreducible C*(G)-image contains the compact operators; consequently C*(G) is GCR, G is type I, and its Mackey and Fell Borel structures agree and are standard.

Assume AC and the fixed KAN Haar measure. The Plancherel measure is carried by nonzero-parameter unitary principal classes and D_n^±, n≥2. Its closed support additionally contains I_(0,0) and D_1^± without atoms, excludes the complementary and trivial classes, and equals the irreducibles weakly contained in the regular representation. The Hilbert–Schmidt transform is onto and gives the regular irreducible disintegration with multiplicity dim H_σ. Formal degrees are (n−1)/(4π).

Assume AC, compact X, divisor D and point p. The coordinate-dependent Laurent coefficient gives an exact sequence 0→O_X(D)→O_X(D+p)→C_p→0. The skyscraper is acyclic, the resulting six-term cohomology sequence is exact, and χ(O_X(D+p))=χ(O_X(D))+1.

Assume AC and integer n≥2. The weighted holomorphic space is Hilbert with bounded point evaluations uniformly on compact subsets. The f_(n,j), j≥0, form a complete orthogonal K-type family with distinct negative-weight characters and multiplicity one; the conjugate model has the positive-weight characters. Character projections give the Hilbert expansion.

Assume AC. For 0<ν<1 the normalized spherical coefficient equals ∫_K |α(p(k,g))|^(1−ν) dk and converges to 1 uniformly on compact subsets as ν↑1. For any sequence increasing to 1, the trivial representation is weakly contained in the corresponding Hilbert direct sum, and the complementary classes converge to the trivial class in the Fell topology.

seams_checked.note: Classification and Plancherel Facts preserve AC, second countability, local compactness, separable carriers, standard measured bases and measurable multiplicity. The Plancherel proof establishes its actual diagonal algebra and onto field model before applying existence and uniqueness interfaces. Its trace-inversion input remains the exact owner-authorized source exception in research/frontier-43-complex-representation-15-conditional-glimm-citation-authorization.json. I corroborated the constants and Haar conversion against Hochs, Theorem 2.1 and §2.6 (https://www.math.ru.nl/~hochs/HC_Plancherel_formula.pdf); original-paper retrieval failed, so I do not claim to have read that original.

Finiteness, the structure-sheaf calculation and nondegeneracy use compact X, holomorphic bundles, compatible supplied metrics and full AC. The smooth Dolbeault quotient is kept separate from maximal Hilbert domains. The harmonic star is conjugate-linear with target K⊗E*, while the integral pairing and induced duality maps are complex-linear in the appropriate variables.

prop-sl2-r-does-not-have-property-t F1, F2 and F8 use exactly the positive weighted complementary completion for 0<ν<1, its unit spherical vector, compact-uniform coefficient convergence and surviving nonzero even K-lines. The proof constructs one direct sum with almost invariant vectors and no invariant vector; it does not infer almost invariance at every fixed parameter.

Read the current divisor-definition uses and the RR uses in differential dimension, point evaluation, trace checking and Jacobi inversion. Compactness, topological genus and full AC are preserved. Canonical-divisor existence is obtained from the supplied RR theorem; O(D) retains its order-bound convention. Jacobi inversion applies RR to degree g to obtain an effective representative, and point evaluation uses ℓ(K−p)=g−1.
